Step 2: use continuity of f for the p-adic topology to conclude that the kernel is a closed submodule of the complete module N. Step 3: use torsion-freeness of M to identify the intersection of the kernel with the p^s-multiples of N as the p^s-multiples of the kernel. Step 4: write the kernel as the inverse limit of the quotients by those submodules and conclude that the induced topology is complete and separated.
